concept: Forward Deployed Engineering: Role And Transition
title: Forward Deployed Engineering: Role And Transition Checkpoint

questions.prompt: A prototype works, but operators still use their spreadsheet. What should the FDE investigate next?

options.label: Workflow fit, reasons for non-use and the intended operational outcome.
Whether a more complex architecture would impress the sponsor.
Whether demo attendance can be counted as completed adoption.

questions.explanation: A working prototype does not establish sustained use. Investigate operator constraints and measure the workflow; architectural novelty and attendance do not show value.

questions.prompt: A frontend engineer is moving into an integration-heavy FDE role. Which practice best addresses a likely gap?

options.label: Rebuild the same interface in three frontend frameworks.
Wait to learn backend boundaries until the first live customer incident.
Build and test a small tenant-aware API, SQL query and fake connector.

questions.explanation: Existing interface skills transfer. A bounded backend/data exercise produces evidence for missing capabilities; framework repetition and deferral leave the gap untested.

questions.prompt: Two companies advertise FDE jobs. Which question best distinguishes their actual roles?

options.label: Do both companies use the same diagram tool?
Who writes production code, owns rollout and supports the customer afterward?
Do both job titles contain the word engineer?

questions.explanation: Ownership across delivery reveals the job shape. Titles and tools do not establish engineering depth, support responsibility or customer exposure.

questions.prompt: You passed all path checkpoints. Which claim is defensible?

options.label: I completed curriculum assessments and can show separate project evidence.
I am certified to operate any customer deployment independently.
My quiz scores predict an offer from a particular employer.

questions.explanation: The assessments measure the authored curriculum. Delivery competence requires separate evidence, and hiring depends on the role and process.
